sections.title: Explanation
sections.content: To express possession, Hungarian commonly uses a possessed noun with a dative possessor and van/vannak.

Notice there's no verb that simply means 'to have' in Hungarian — van egy könyvem is literally 'my book exists', with the possessor built into the noun. The dative pronoun (nekem, 'to me') is grammatically there but gets dropped constantly in casual speech, just like subject pronouns do.
